label: copy-phase input k (re-fed k)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and only on steps where the input is the token k (the model's own fed-back k). On dev, 99.98% of activations and essentially all activation mass are on copy-phase k inputs. It never fires during the original phase (including on k there), at the delimiter, or on any other input token apart from a handful of near-zero y/a cases. It fires on only about 43% of copy-phase k inputs, though. I found nothing that cleanly separates firing from non-firing k steps. Position (recall_idx, to_go), out_tok, in_count, digits and first_tok each change precision only slightly (0.30-0.50). out_tok == k (repeated kk) is the exception: precision 0.70, but it covers only 5% of activations. Earlier tokens such as f, p or h raise precision a little (about 0.50), so the gating seems to depend on distributed hidden-state content. On magnitude: the largest activations come on k that sits late in long sequences (copy steps 13-17, e.g. orig index 5-6 when L=9). Small activations show up on k at early recall positions, and firing rate rises with t.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: k, y, a, -, v, n; least: m, q, h, <DEL>) and the next token to output (most: r, 3, z, f, p, h; least: w, y, q, a); timing cues that raise it most: L=4 & t=7, L=5 & t=9, recall_idx=7.
